summary: A 1977 Telnet option that lets a user log out cleanly, so one side can ask the other to end the session. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 727 defines a TELNET option for asking the remote host to log out a user process instead of leaving it detached. The same option can warn that a server plans to log out an inactive process.

subtitle: A TELNET option that lets one side request a forced logout of the remote user process.

tldr.problem: A connection close may detach a user's process instead of ending it, while normal logout can be slow or impossible for a hung process.
tldr.mechanism: The LOGOUT option, code 18, lets a user request that the server forcibly log out its process, or lets a server warn about an impending automatic logout.
tldr.outcome: RFC 727 is a Proposed Standard and defines a default in which neither side requests forcible logout.

today: RFC 727 is a Proposed Standard. The unit lists no updates or obsoleting RFCs.

sections.title: Why Ask for a Forced Logout
sections.content:
A user process may hang so it cannot be interrupted, or the host may respond so slowly that the user wants to leave. Closing the connection does not always end the process: many hosts detach it so the user can reconnect without losing work after an accidental close.

If the user is giving up on the host, a detached hung process may continue to consume resources. The LOGOUT option provides a way to request that the server forcibly log out the process instead of detaching it.
sections.plainLanguage: Closing a connection can leave the user's process running on the host. The option lets the user ask the host to end that process instead.

sections.title: LOGOUT Commands and Default
sections.content:
The option is named LOGOUT and has code 18. IAC DO LOGOUT asks the receiver to forcibly log out the user process at its end, while IAC WILL LOGOUT requests or confirms permission for the sender to do so at its end.

IAC DON'T LOGOUT demands that the receiver not forcibly log out its process, and IAC WON'T LOGOUT refuses to do so. The default is WON'T LOGOUT and DON'T LOGOUT, meaning no forcible logout.
sections.plainLanguage: DO asks the other side to log out its process; WILL agrees to a logout request. DON'T and WON'T refuse or prevent forced logout.

sections.title: Logging Out Without Waiting
sections.content:
A user who does not want to wait for the normal logout procedure sends IAC DO LOGOUT. The server may reply IAC WILL LOGOUT and begin logging out the process immediately. It need not wait for the user to receive confirmation or close the connection itself.

The RFC says an impatient user may send the request and then close the connection; a server that implements the option should still process the request. If the server refuses with WON'T LOGOUT, a later connection break may leave the process detached.
sections.plainLanguage: The server can start the logout as soon as it agrees, even if the user closes the connection before seeing the reply. If it refuses, the process may be detached instead.

sections.title: Warning About Automatic Logout
sections.content:
A server may use IAC WILL LOGOUT to warn that it is approaching its automatic logout time for an inactive user. The user can respond with IAC DON'T LOGOUT and continue working.

The RFC also says this warning does not prevent the server from logging out the process if inactivity continues. This prevents a user from keeping a process indefinitely by repeatedly refusing a warning without resuming work.
sections.plainLanguage: A server can warn an inactive user that logout is near. The user can continue working, but simply refusing the warning does not prevent logout if inactivity continues.
